According to the Brighton criteria provided, Doppler ultrasound is a valid imaging study for confirming DVT. The text also mentions surgical thrombectomy with intraoperative confirmation, but this is a therapeutic procedure, not one of the specific diagnostic imaging modalities listed in options 1-4 (though it confirms the diagnosis, the question asks to select studies from the list that confirmed DVT; typically, imaging studies are selected here. However, looking at the options, "Doppler/Duplex Ultrasound" is explicitly listed as option 4). The text does not mention CT venography, MR venography, or contrast catheter venography. While "Compression ultrasonography" (Option 1) and "Doppler/Duplex Ultrasound" (Option 4) are related, the text specifically says "ecocolordoppler", which maps directly to Option 4. In many clinical contexts, these are used together, but based on the specific terminology "color Doppler", Option 4 is the most precise match for the modality described. Some classifications might group them, but given they are separate options, we must choose the one explicitly named. The text says "ecocolordoppler", which is Doppler ultrasound. It does not explicitly state "compression" was the primary method, though it is often part of the exam. However, Option 4 "Doppler/Duplex Ultrasound" is a direct synonym for "ecocolordoppler".

A thrombus is a localized hemostatic plug or blood clot in a
blood vessel. Thrombosis occurs when a thrombus causes blockage
in the blood vessel. This blockage can result in partial or complete
blood ﬂow obstruction either in larger vessels such as arteries or
veins, or smaller vessels collectively termed as microcirculation.

sites will be speciﬁed, as appropriate. Thromboembolism is an

C.brighton_context:
Normal D-dimer levels help to rule out DVT and PE in patients
with a low probability for DVT or PE but not in patients who have
a high probability [78]. The D-dimer test has high sensitivity (80–
100 %) but low speciﬁcity (23–63 %) [79]. Despite its widespread
use as a biomarker, the D-dimer test has several limitations. There
is marked variability in the methodology used, making it difﬁcult
to have a reference standard. In patients older than 50 years, an
age-adjusted threshold should be used as normal D-dimer levels
increase with age [79]. Troponin and B-type natriuretic peptide
(BNP) are biomarkers of cardiac injury and can be used to assess
the severity of PE.
